newsitem.title: USA: Aon sees large deal unlikely in short term.
newsitem.headline: Aon sees large deal unlikely in short term.

text.p: Aon Corp chief executive Patrick Ryan told analysts in a conference call on Thursday that the company is unlikely to make a large acquisition in the next year or so.
However, the Chicago-based insurance broker still plans to make smaller-scale purchases as part of its growth strategy, he said.
Aon has already purchased three of its larger rivals in the last six months, stretching its ability to manage another large deal, he told analysts.

Aon in October spent about $250 million to buy U.K. broker Bain Hogg, the eleventh largest broker in the world, and then two months later agreed to spend about $1.23 billion to buy Alexander & Alexander, the fourth largest broker in the world.
Just last month, Aon agreed to buy Minet Group from St. Paul Cos Inc for an undisclosed price.
"I would expect that we will continue in '97 and on in '98 doing the kinds of acquisitions we normally do, outside of the very large ones," he told analysts on the conference call.
"That is because of the assimilation and integration of what we have, and that is somewhat financial related," he said on a replay of the tape recorded call.
However, he said the company has been working on some acquisition opportunities.
But, "if you're asking, 'Are we going to do a giant?', the probability of that is quite low, in that time," he said, referring to the 1997-1998 time period.
In a telephone interview with Reuters on Thursday, Ryan said he did not believe the company's resources were stretched by the recent acquisitions.
In that interview, Ryan said Aon was capable of making additional acquisitions, but did not discuss whether the company was able to do more large deals.
When asked in the interview if Aon would consider making an offer for Willis Corroon Group Plc or Sedgwick Group Plc, Ryan declined to comment.

Willis Corroon and Sedgwick have been the subject of much speculation in recent weeks following a wave of consolidation in the insurance brokerage industry that has put them far behind industry giants Aon and Marsh & McLennan Cos Inc.
Merrill Lynch analyst Jay Cohen said he doubts Aon will make a bid for either Willis Corroon or Sedgwick.
"There had been rumors floating about that they were going to be making a fairly sizable acquisition and he tried to put that to rest," Cohen said of Ryan's comments on the conference call.
However, Cohen said, Aon may be in the market to buy smaller, specialized brokers to help boost its growth.
In the call Thursday, Ryan said he expects organic growth for the total merged brokerage service operation of more than 3 percent, down from its historical rate of about six percent.
He said he believes the company can return to close to its historical rate of organic growth after 1998.
